items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: We put a band together for Kid Howard and Kid was here for a while.

ctx.x: And what have you been playing most nights a week?

Six nights a week. Six nights a week. When he came in as a steady band, you see. And opposed to George, we had Lizzie Miles whom we resurrected. And Lizzie would do, along with Joe Robichaud, she would do the low, you know, the 15 minutes. And of course we went through many, many wonderful people like Kid Howard. We put a band together for Kid Howard and Kid was here for a while. About that time his chops came out and he had to take a respite from it. We were probably using it.

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: Because when I was on Bourbon Street after some time back I had my own band at the Mardi Gras for quite a while out there for Sid.

ctx.x: Yeah. Tom or somebody. Punch. Yeah. I could play some tapes of him, but I'd better not. I think his lip was down when he made those records.

I'll tell you about him, he just lost interest in it. He don't like to play. That's for sure. Because when I was on Bourbon Street after some time back I had my own band at the Mardi Gras for quite a while out there for Sid. And then I played on Tuesdays with the band and I got him out there and he said it was all right until he gets on the stand and he found all kind of fault. He just don't like to play it.
Well there's very few guys who can play both alto and clarinet I notice. Well I don't know. Not too many of them can do it. I know it don't seem to bother Contrell.
